channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Nearly 1.7 million deaths linked to second-hand smoke in 2023, study finds
item.description: More than 2.7 billion people worldwide, including 767 million children, were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to nearly 1.7 million deaths, a Lancet study said on Tuesday. Researchers found second-hand smoke remained a major global health risk, with no safe level of exposure.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Eiffel Tower closed in row over women removed for Hindu group
item.description: The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday because of a strike by staff over the removal of female colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group, workers and management said. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: EU says no place for 'glorification of war criminals' as Mladic buried
item.description: The European Union on Monday denounced any "glorification" of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic in Serbia, as thousands gathered in Belgrade for his funeral. FRANCE 24's James Vasina reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israel intensifies South Lebanon strikes, killing 13 after weeks-long lull
item.description: Israel launched a wave of airstrikes across southern Lebanon, killing 13 people, including women and children, Lebanon’s health ministry said on Monday, marking an escalation after weeks of relative calm. Israel said it would continue targeting Iran-backed Hezbollah over alleged ceasefire violations. Hezbollah has not commented on the strikes.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Volkswagen's Osnabrück plant to switch from cars to defence
item.description: Crisis-hit Volkswagen has struck a preliminary deal to sell its Osnabrück plant in Lower Saxony to the state government and Israeli investor Aurelius Capital. From mid 2027, the iconic factory is expected to start producing equipment for Rafael Advanced Defence Systems, the company behind the Iron Dome missile defence system. But first, a look at the state of the German economy following far-right AfD's historic election win in Saxony-Anhalt.
item.dc:creator: Yuka ROYER

item.title: Egyptian influencer's death penalty over drug charges
item.description: In tonight's edition, a South African high court rejects a former defence minister's bid to have a corruption case against her dropped. Also, an Egyptian TV presenter is amongst a dozen people the court has sentenced to death on drug charges. And the very first Pan-African Architecture Biennale opened its doors on Monday in the Kenyan capital.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Only the beginning? German far-right's breakthrough shakes Europe to its core
item.description: Not enough to win outright but enough to shake Germany and Europe to their core: the far-right Alterniv für Deutschland trouncing the ruling conservatives in the impoverished former East German region of Saxony-Anhalt. We’ll ask about the consequences of voting for an anti-immigrant, pro-Russian party that wants schools to teach less about the ills of Hitler and more the glory of Bismarck.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: 'Polarised Brazil': Lula remains a ‘strong candidate’ despite the challenges of incumbency
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andreza Aruska de Souza Santos, Director of King’s Brazil Institute at the School of Global Affairs, King’s College London and Associate Professor in Brazil and Latin American Studies. According to Aruska, Brazil’s approaching elections can be viewed through the following prism: macroeconomic performance and political confidence are moving on different tracks. While headline indicators may suggest an economy performing relatively well, she argues that many Brazilians experience a much harsher reality shaped by the cost of living and a volatile job market.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Tunisians tell the story of their summer of shortages
item.description: Frequent water and power cuts, long queues for bottled water, poultry farms destroyed by the heat: these have been the scenes across Tunisia this summer as millions of people were affected by shortages in electricity and water. Our Observers say this is the result of years of underinvestment in infrastructure while the Tunisian president, for his part, blames "deliberate and planned acts of sabotage”.
item.dc:creator: The FRANCE 24 Observers

item.title: 'What we see right now is that Putin has zero interest in ending the war', Ukrainian MP Yasko says
item.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff on Monday touted progress in weekend discussions with Ukraine and Russia, raising the prospect of reviving three-way peace talks to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II. Ukrainian MP Lisa Yasko says that "we don't trust these talks", describing the US envoys' flattery towards Russian President Vladimir Putin as "disgraceful".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israel warns of 'full-scale war' if Palestinian Authority launches Oct. 7-style attack
item.description: Israel on Monday threatened a “full-scale war” against the Palestinian Authority if it believed the West Bank-based body was preparing an attack on Israeli forces or settlements resembling Hamas’s October 7, 2023 assault. The warning was denounced by Palestinian authorities as an attempt to fuel the conflict during the Israeli election season.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Eiffel Tower workers go on strike after female staff 'sidelined' for Hindu group's visit
item.description: The Eiffel Tower was forced to close on Monday after staff went on strike to protest the "sidelining" and "replacement" of female employees during a recent visit by a Hindu delegation. The Paris landmark's operator said the group had requested that the private visit be organised in such a way as to limit "interactions with women".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Avalanche kills at least 11 climbers in southern Russia
item.description: ⁠At least ​11 people were killed and six ​others injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in Russia's ​southern Kabardino-Balkaria ‌Republic, local emergency services said. The ‌avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, ⁠one of the highest peaks in Russia's North Caucasus.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Will AfD win in Germany boost France's far right?
item.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party on the cusp of power at state level for the first time since World War Two. The result has garnered attention across Europe, not least in France where national elections next year could see far-right veteran Marine Le Pen become president.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Macron hosts summit to urge support for cinema amid impact of AI, streaming
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday called for stronger international efforts to protect cinema from the disruptive impact of artificial intelligence and streaming platforms while hosting more than 200 industry figures at the Lumière Summit in southern France.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon kill 11
item.description: Israeli strikes ⁠on a ​southern Lebanese town early on Monday killed at least 11 people including two children ​and two medics, Lebanon's state news agency said. Israel has intensified its bombardment of south Lebanon in recent days despite a June ceasefire that was meant ​to halt fighting ‌between the Israeli military and Lebanese armed ⁠group Hezbollah.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Céline Dion and Jay-Z bring their hits to Paris
item.description: In this edition of our arts24 music show, Jennifer Ben Brahim brings us a roundup of some of the week's most anticipated Paris concerts. From Céline Dion kicking off her 16 sold-out shows at La Défense Arena, to American rapper Jay-Z celebrating his 30-year career at the Stade de France, we've got you covered.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer BEN BRAHIM

item.title: What now for Germany's Merz after AfD win?
item.description: The far-right AfD's triumph in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt marks a defeat for German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and sends a warning to other European leaders battling the same mixture of slow growth and disillusion with mainstream politics. In an increasingly polarized political system, Merz, whose personal approval ratings have sunk ‌to record lows, was one of the main targets of voter ire over the cost of living, pensions and economic insecurity. France 24’s Philip Turle takes a look at what the AfD’s victory means for the German leader and for Europe.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Saxony-Anhalt poll: 'A huge blow for the CDU, but also a huge win for the AfD'
item.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Markus Ziener, Visiting Senior Fellow at the German Marshall Fund. He interprets the AfD’s breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt as a potentially historic turning point in post-war German politics. For Ziener, the significance lies not only in the scale of the far right’s electoral success, but also in the constituency behind it: many AfD voters, he argues, were previously politically disengaged rather than simply defecting from established parties. This complicates conventional explanations of the result as a straightforward transfer of support from the CDU to the AfD and raises a deeper question about the political expectations of a newly mobilised electorate.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: How far-right AfD breakthrough may ‘cause absolute chaos’ in Germany
item.description: Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) came out well ahead in Sunday’s regional elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, becoming the first far-right party to come close to gaining power at the regional level since World War II. The lead candidate of the party in the state, Ulrich Siegmund, said Monday that his party had already initiated talks towards building a governing majority.
item.dc:creator: Simon FEISTHAUER FOURNET

item.title: Two children among dead in Israeli strikes on Lebanon
item.description: Israeli airstrikes overnight killed 11 people in a south Lebanon village, including two infants, Lebanese state media said Monday, a day after separate raids left seven dead. France 24's Renée Davis in Beirut has the latest.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: REPLAY: 'Shocked' Merz speaks after far-right election victory
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Monday he was "deeply shocked" after his centre-right party suffered a heavy loss in a state poll to the far-right AfD, but vowed to push on with reforms. Watch his press conference in full above.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘Idiots and traitors’: World reacts to AfD’s election victory
item.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday. The result puts a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time in the country since World War II. The outcome has European capitals taking notice, particularly in France where the campaign for next year's presidential elections has gotten underway.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: UN rapporteur says Israeli rubble-clearing in Gaza could erase 'atrocity crimes' evidence
item.description: The United Nations Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese warned on Monday that the large-scale rubble removal in parts of Gaza under Israeli control could risk erasing "evidence relevant to the investigation of alleged international crimes".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
